text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Hebron deal almost complete. Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon clash over security details.
- Mordechai finds warmth in Egypt.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must calm waters of his troubled coalition.
- Two Egoz unit soldiers killed in Lebanon.
- Red Cross documents reveal how much it knew of Nazi atrocities.
- Women attack government retreat on tax benefits.
- Dovrat-Shrem raise additional $32 million for Polaris venture capital fund.
- Bezeq Communications launches "Intelligent Network".
- Antitrust authority director-general Yoram Turbowicz: Direct Insurance, Bank Leumi should have separate boards.
- Housing Minister Meir Porush attacks Treasury proposals for foreign labour.
- Government to float 17-20 percent of Bank Discount in February.
- Teva estimates potential sales of multiple-sclerosis drug Copaxone at $100 million next year.
GLOBES
- Expected budget deficit of three billion shekels in December.
- Israel and Cable and Wireless consider setting up joint company that would hold 20 percent of Bezeq.
- 11 percent rise in sale of new apartments in cities in third quarter.
HAARETZ
- Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak tells Mordechai: There's no place for talk of war between us.
- Work slowdown expected tomorrow at Bezeq, airports, ports and rails authorities.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Two soldiers killed by roadside bomb in Lebanon.
- Netanyahu: Hebron deal nearly done.
MAARIV
- Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon in fight against the Hebron agreement.
- Labour party leader Shimon Peres to visit Likud HQ in January.
